thread:
PagerDuty Bot: PAGER: serving-runtime-latency-spike (SEV2) -> paging eng-runtime oncall. link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-7890

Maria: ack - I'm on it. seeing a big 99th percentile token latency jump in us-west.

Maria: quick numbers: p99 token latency went from ~120ms to ~2.4s in the last 4m, error rate +9% (5xxs).

RuntimeSvc Bot: recent logs (excerpts):
```
2024-08-01T04:12:08Z ERROR gpu_executor: cuda runtime error: out of memory at /opt/runtime/gpu_executor.cu:198
2024-08-01T04:12:09Z WARN batching: observed batch_size 2300 > configured_target 64, backlog=4500
2024-08-01T04:12:09Z ERROR serve: container "runtimesvc" terminated with exit_code 137
```

Samir: @Maria can you confirm whether this is continuous batching growing unbounded or a separate memory leak? logs show OOM + immediate restarts.

Maria: initial read: looks like the batching queue accumulated a huge backlog, batch size ballooned, GPUs OOMed, kube restarted pods, then node flaps started.

Jen: SRE view - we're seeing 2 nodes in us-west-2b with repeated OOMKills for runtimesvc, kubelet showing repeated restart loops on those pods.

Liam: infra - pulling node-level metrics, memory saturation on those hosts aligns with the timing of the backlog. I can cordon the most affected node to stop scheduling until we mitigate.

Maria: immediate mitigations proposed: 
- temporarily lower continuous batching max_batch_size from 4096 -> 128
- lower batching window from 200ms -> 30ms
- enable the CPU fallback routing policy for affected model families
- add +2 replicas to runtime deployment to absorb load
- roll these changes to a 10% canary first
- if situation doesn't improve, toggle feature-flag to disable continuous batching entirely

Samir: applying configmap patch and initiating canary rollout. Running these commands: 
```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/runtimesvc BATCH_MAX=128 BATCH_WINDOW_MS=30
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/runtimesvc --replicas=12 --selector=canary=false
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/runtimesvc -l canary=true
```

Support Triage: noting impacted customers: 11 customers saw elevated latency alerts; 1 enterprise (BlueStone) opened a support ticket. Estimated approx 0.9% of overall traffic in us-west impacted during spike.

Maria: cordoning node ip-10-1-23-87 and beginning drain to prevent further restarts.

Liam: cordon+drain done (commands: kubectl cordon ip-10-1-23-87; kubectl drain ip-10-1-23-87 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data). Observed fewer restarts after drain.

Samir: canary telemetry: canary pods show queue length down ~65%, no new OOMs in canary. Rolling canary to 100%.

RuntimeSvc Bot: post-rollout checks: OOM log lines dropped to 0 in last 10m; p99 latency back to ~160-200ms; container restarts reduced to zero in last 12m.

Maria: good work. keeping feature-flag disable on standby. For now low batch sizes and smaller window will remain until RCA complete.

Support Triage: account team notified BlueStone; proposed SLA credit window 2024-08-01T04:10Z-04:40Z. Draft statuspage update prepared.

Samir: initial root cause hypothesis: bug in continuous batching backlog-handling where on pod restart there was no backpressure signaling to upstream request queue. After restart, pending requests re-enqueued, consumers allowed to create extremely large batches (no hard cap), leading to GPU OOMs and container crashes. Also found a secondary condition: when batch consumers are starved by large batches, a deadlock can occur causing queue starvation and cascading latency.

Jen: SRE notes: paging thresholds reviewed — current alert triggers on p95 > 1s; suggest lowering batch-related alerts to catch earlier (batch_size > 512, queue_length > 1000). I'll update runbook and alerts.

Samir: action items (owners):
- Samir: reproduce with stress harness simulating pod restarts mid-backlog; add integration test for backpressure behavior
- Samir: implement runtime hard cap on batch_size (e.g., 1024) and a circuit-breaker that rejects/redirects when queue growth > 500
- Maria: update incident runbook with clear steps for batching incidents and paging thresholds
- Jen: update alerting rules (batch_size high, queue growth) and validate on staging
- Liam: ticket to review autoscaling policies to prevent immediate node saturation on pod restarts (INFRA-792)

Maria: I'll hand off to Samir for deep-dive and RCA. My on-call shift ends in 18m; I'll remain available for questions.

Samir: taking ownership of RCA. I'll post timelines and the RCA draft in this thread.

Ops Bot: incident INC-7890 status -> mitigated; monitoring. Severity: SEV2 pending RCA.

Maria: closing pager for now. Please keep this thread updated with any regressions. Continue monitoring for 1 hour before marking resolved.

Liam: one follow-up - consider adding an immediate safety guard in the scheduler to prevent single-pod restarts from letting backlog requeue uncontrollably. Filing INFRA-793.

Support Triage: posted customer notifications and updated statuspage draft.

Samir: timeline summary for RCA: first OOM observed 2024-08-01T04:12:08Z; mitigations applied 04:18Z; full rollout of safer batching parameters 04:26Z; metrics normalized by 04:35Z. Will include logs, heap dumps, and test reproductions in RCA doc.

Maria: thanks team. :thumbsup: keeping monitoring until 05:35Z then will propose incident resolved if stable.
